prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
competitors_mentioned: Require a Manual J Load Calculation
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one universal “best” — the right company depends on your home, budget, equipment preference, and whether you want the lowest price or best long‑term performance/warranty. I can help you pick the right contractor for your situation if you tell me your ZIP code, home size/age, and whether you want a standard AC or a heat pump.

Below is a practical, fast way to find the best Atlanta HVAC contractor to replace your air conditioner.

What to do (step‑by‑step)
1. Get 3 written quotes
   - From three different licensed Atlanta HVAC contractors. Compare item‑by‑item (equipment, SEER, labor warranty, permits, ductwork, refrigerant, disposal).
2. Require a Manual J load calculation
   - Any reputable contractor will perform or provide a Manual J heat/load calculation to size the system properly. If they just “eyeball” the size, walk away.
3. Check credentials
   - Verify Georgia HVAC license (and city/county permits if required), proof of insurance, and local reviews (Google, BBB, Nextdoor). Ask for recent references in your neighborhood.
4. Ask specific questions
   - Exact equipment brand/model and SEER rating
   - Included components (condensing unit, evaporator coil, thermostat, refrigerant, line set, pad)
   - Labor warranty length and what it covers
   - Manufacturer’s warranty registration and who services the unit under warranty
   - Whether duct modifications are needed and the cost
   - Who pulls permits and handles inspections
   - Estimated timeline and payment schedule
5. Compare apples to apples
   - Ensure quoted systems are comparable (same tonnage, SEER, coil type, accessory features). Lower price may mean lower efficiency, shorter warranties, or omitted work.
6. Watch for red flags
   - Huge cash‑only discounts, high‑pressure sales, unwillingness to show license/insurance, no written contract, very short warranty, or refusal to perform Manual J.

What to expect on price (ballpark)
- Typical full replacement for a common single‑family home in Atlanta: roughly $4,000–$12,000.
   - Lower end: basic 2–3 ton midgrade system with simple install
   - Higher end: high‑efficiency 16–20+ SEER heat pumps or complex installs, ductwork replacement, or multi‑story homes can be $8k–$15k+
- Exact price depends on size (tons), SEER, brand, complexity of install, need for new ductwork, and local labor.

Brands to consider
- Reputable mainstream brands: Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Rheem/Ruud, Bryant, American Standard, Goodman (value). Also consider high‑efficiency heat pumps if you want efficiency and possible rebates.
- Don’t choose purely by brand—installation quality is often more important than nameplate.

Rebates, incentives & refrigerant
- Check current federal/state/local incentives for high‑efficiency heat pumps (these change frequently).
- Newer systems may use newer refrigerants; ask contractor which refrigerant and future serviceability.

How I can help right now
- If you give your ZIP code (and any preferences like brand, budget, or whether you want a heat pump), I’ll:
  - Suggest 3–5 well‑reviewed contractors in your area to contact
  - Provide a customized list of questions or a comparison worksheet you can use when you get quotes

Want me to find a short list of local contractors for your ZIP code?
